newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to ask Germany to recoup millions in TV duties.
newsitem.headline: EU to ask Germany to recoup millions in TV duties.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to tell Germany on Wednesday to recoup about 10 million marks in unpaid customs duties on imports of television sets assembled in Turkey, Commission and industry sources said.
The decision follows complaints from rival manufacturers that TV sets entered Germany at abnormally low prices between 1991 and 1994.
"Our investigation concluded...that German importers had simply not paid the customs duties they should have," a Commission official told Reuters.
At issue was the payment of duties on imports of television parts into Turkey from non-EU countries.

Under an agreement with the EU, the Turkish government should have charged a 14-percent tariff on imports of such parts used in sets intended for the European market. But due to a legal loophole the goods entered the country free of charge until 1994, an industry source said.
Alternatively, the German importers should have made a compensatory payment.
The unfairly low-priced sets are said to have harmed sales in Germany of Grundig, its Dutch parent Philips and France's Thomson, the industry source said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6841
